hints: Notice the question asks for the definition, not a formula that can be used to calculate potential difference in a special case.
Recall the base quantities involved in voltage: energy transferred by electrical work $W$ in joules and charge $Q$ in coulombs.
Check which option matches $V = W/Q$ with unit $\text{J C}^{-1}$, and separate it from $V = IR$, $V = P/I$ and $V = Ed$.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the general definition of potential difference between two points, valid for any circuit or field.
State the governing definition: potential difference is energy converted per unit charge, $V = W/Q$, where $W$ is work done in $\text{J}$ and $Q$ is charge in $\text{C}$.
Check units: $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ J C}^{-1}$, which confirms work done per unit charge.

Compare the other statements: $V = IR$ needs a resistance, $V = P/I$ comes from $P = VI$, and $V = Ed$ needs a uniform field of strength $E$ over distance $d$, so each is a special-case result, not the definition.
Therefore work done per unit charge is the definition. This is option D

options.A: Since $P = VI$, $P/I$ does equal $V$ numerically, but it is a rearranged power relation, not the definition of potential difference.
options.B: Since $V = IR$, the product $IR$ can calculate $V$ for a resistor, but it is Ohm's law, not the general definition.
options.C: Since $V = Ed$, the product $Ed$ gives $V$ only for a uniform electric field, not the general definition.
options.D: Potential difference is defined by $V = W/Q$, the work done $W$ moving charge $Q$ between two points, measured in $\text{J C}^{-1}$ or volts.
